After discussing with @Moritz Firsching, I'm running a new version of the pipeline on FC c90271f0fa9 (latest right now). I will try to filter out from the website ones that already have an issue or PR open.

FYI, changes in the new pipeline version:

  • No ForMathlib files by default. The 170 library files are skipped, as they just created duplicate reports.
  • Trivial proof phase after the review. When misformalizations are reported, the same agent may write one short Lean file outside the checkout at /workspace/review/evidence.lean proving or refuting the statements as formalized; bailing out is allowed.
  • Fix phase still runs after the evidence phase
  • Negative examples. Hand-written cases that should not be flagged (currently Erdős 295 and Erdős 431, both "reformulation") ship into /workspace/examples/not_misformalizations/.
  • Website can show runs at different revisions. The website now records each run under its FC sha (/fc-review-results/<short sha>/), existing links still work and redirect to 84063d6942.

I ran a new misformalization review on FC 782312817c (today's main): https://tadamcz.com/fc-review-results/782312817c/

44 alleged misformalizations in 32 files (1382 problem files reviewed), down from 209 in 139 files on c90271f0 ten days ago. Congratulations, especially to @Moritz Firsching and @Salvatore Mercuri , on clearing the queue so fast.

The share of reviewed files with at least one misformalization fell from 11% (139 of 1268) in the previous review to 2% (32 of 1382) now :tada:. 2% may be at the noise threshold, I guess we'll see?

I compared the 44 findings with the c90271f0 review:

  • 17 findings are in 11 files added since the previous review. All were Erdos problems files. This suggests a relatively high rate of errors in newly added Erdos files, see below.
  • 10 findings concern a problem the previous review did notice but classified as questionable, minor, a status issue or a reformulation. This time the reviewer calls them misformalizations. Examples: Erdős 1067 has answer(False) although Thomassen proved the statement, and Erdős 44 uses the integer N.sqrt / 2 where the source has √N/2. I think we're seeing some inevitable noise here on cases that are difficult for the model to judge.
  • 7 findings were not reported in any form by the previous review, although it did check those files. We don't know whether the new or the old review is correct.
  • 10 findings repeat a misformalization that the previous review already reported. Nine of them are covered by PRs that are still awaiting review: FC#5350 (Erdős 897, five findings), FC#5543, FC#5452, FC#5519, FC#5512. The tenth, Paper/Homogenous, has open issue FC#5699.

There is a high flag rate in the new Erdos additions. Since the c90271f0 review, 114 problem files were added, 100 of them Erdős problems. Of those 100 new Erdős files, 11 were flagged (11%), against 21 of the 1263 pre-existing files (1.7%). The other 14 additions were all clean. So the new Erdős batch is flagged at roughly the rate the whole repository had before the fixing wave

I ran the review again at aea251bb (23 September at 11am), this time with Opus 5.5 (all previous runs used GPT-6 Astra). The model has a different style, and flagged some additional files.

Results: 64 files flagged out of 1403 (4.5%).

https://tadamcz.com/fc-review-results/aea251bb26/#/

I do want to emphasise again that an AI flagging more files doesn't necessarily mean it's more correct. They may be false positives. Don't trust the AI output blindly. Now that the more "obvious" ones have been found and fixed, it may be wise to do more real manual spot-checking on whether you still think (as in the workshop week) that the AI flags actually check out.

One notable style difference is Opus tries much harder to find "trivial proofs" for statements it thinks are misformalized (at a rate of 42/64, much higher than Astra).

The disagreement between Opus and Astra is almost entirely one-directional. Among files unchanged between the two commits, only 1 that Astra flagged is not flagged by Opus (Erdős 1108, which Opus downgraded to questionable).

Examples (described by AI) below

  • Erdős 1030. Opus: the Lean requires the ratio R(k+1,k)/R(k,k) to converge to a limit greater than 1, while the Burr–Erdős conjecture only asks that it stay bounded away from 1; a proof of the conjecture would not prove the Lean statement, and a proof that the ratio oscillates would refute the Lean without touching the problem. Astra: "the cited problem explicitly uses an ordinary limit", faithful, nothing to report. This one is a genuine judgment call about how literally to read Erdős.
  • Erdős 11. Opus: erdosproblems.com changed the question on 2026-04-05 from "every odd n" to "every large odd n", and the file still states the universal version, which is strictly stronger. Astra checked six declarations, ran a sieve to five million, and found no defect. Astra did not notice the source revision.
  • Erdős 1134, Klarner variant. Opus: the Lean set is seeded with 0 where Klarner's problem in every cited paper is seeded with 1, and the two closures differ (3 is in one, 5 in the other, verified in Lean). Astra looked at the same declaration and recorded only a reformulation about lower density versus density.
  • Wikipedia/Koethe, Amitsur's conjecture. Opus: the declaration asserts Amitsur's conjecture as a solved theorem, but the conjecture is false (Smoktunowicz's nil algebra), and the file's own docstring says so; the negation should wrap the quantifier over rings. Astra recorded the same declaration as a reformulation ("J[x] is represented by TwoSidedIdeal.map") and two minor docstring items.
  • OEIS/153330, Conjecture 4. Opus: quantifying over every integer m, including values that never occur in the sequence, makes the ratio 0/0 and the limit false; it proved in Lean that the file's Conjecture 3 and Conjecture 4 formalizations are mutually inconsistent. Astra saw the same declaration and called it questionable, on a different ground (the sign-symmetry of the exclusion list).
  • Books/Bugeaud Problem 10.6, both variants. Opus says both research open statements are elementary theorems and reports proving each one verbatim in Lean (70 and 320 lines), e.g. the "genuinely sublacunary" growth condition still admits an explicit dense sequence. Astra checked all eleven declarations, found no misformalization, and noted only a misleading docstring and two reformulations. Its notes say the book leaves "very rapidly increasing" unquantified and the solvability was reported as a status matter.
Also, Opus is capable of giving confidence judgements for its claims (unlike Astra which nearly always says its confidence is about p=0.99 or p=1, haha!)

There were also a few cases where AI flagged a change that was previously made in response to an AI misformalization review.

For example the below on Erdos 951, which may be a cautionary tale, could people take a look?

Erdos 951 story (AI-written)

7 Sept, first audit (Astra). The Beurling variant in 951.lean said: for any Beurling prime system, if the count of generalised integers up to x is x + o(log x), the generators are the primes. The reviewer showed it was false as stated: BeurlingIntegers a is the set of product values, so multiplicities are lost. With generators 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, … the set of values is all positive integers, the count is ⌊x⌋, and a₂ = 4 is not the third prime.

10 Sept, FC#5464. Jack's fix (drafted with Claude Code, citing the audit) came with a compiling Lean disproof of the old statement, which is great. But the fix itself was to add the separation hypothesis Erdos951Prop a (distinct generalised integers differ by at least 1) to the variant, with the justification that the source states Beurling's conjecture for such sequences. Moritz approved and merged it within six hours.

11 Sept, next audit, one day later. The reviewer noticed that in Erdős's survey [Er80] Beurling's conjecture is stated for an arbitrary increasing sequence, and unit separation only appears in the following paragraph, for Shapiro's separate question (13). So the merged fix had narrowed Beurling's conjecture to a special case. It filed this as "questionable", not a misformalization, so nothing happened. The 21 Sept review said the same, again at "questionable".

23 Sept, Opus 5.5. Same observation, but it goes further and claims the narrowed statement is now trivially true: under unit separation, density one already forces the generalised integers to be all of ℕ and hence the generators to be the primes, so Beurling's o(log x) threshold plays no role. Its suggested fix is to count exponent vectors with multiplicity, i.e. what the first finding actually implied, and it warns that just deleting the hypothesis reproduces the original falsity. It did not manage a compiling proof of its triviality claim, and rates its own confidence at 0.68.

On OEIS/103662, Opus provided a "trivial proof" but I think it's quite plausible this is just a correct proof of the corrected statement? It's a pretty obscure sequence and the OEIS authors probably didn't try very hard to prove it. There's a lot of pretty unremarkable conjectures in the OEIS, if OEIS Open (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11941) is any indication.

OEIS 103662 summary (AI-written)

OEIS/103662. The 11 Sept review said the conjecture demanded that every large exponent lack a zeroless power, where OEIS only conjectures that some exponent does (the entry defines "finite" that way and says a(40) is unknown). FC#5758 restated it faithfully as ∃ n, a n = 0. The 23 Sept review then proved it: for n = 2500 = λ(10⁵), every b > 1 has b^2500 ending in 00001, 09376, …0625 or 0, so there is always a zero digit. Sorry-free 90-line proof against the current commit. https://tadamcz.com/fc-review-results/aea251bb26/#/f/OEIS/103662
btw, the OEIS does make me wonder whether additions like FC#6426 or FC#4946 are worth the maintenance burden.

Two other cases where a "fix" might have been wrong, or thrown up deeper issues, please take a look

AI-written

GraphConjecture23. The 11 Sept review said conjecture23 averaged vertex-to-M distances where WOWII means something else. FC#5736 introduced distAvgSet, the average distance between distinct vertices within M. The 23 Sept review says the source's d(M,V) is the average of nonzero distances from M to all vertices, so the fix landed on a third definition, and it gives a 23-vertex graph where the fixed Lean inequality fails while the source's holds. The two reviews contradict each other, so at least one is wrong. Someone with the WOWII glossary open could settle it quickly. https://tadamcz.com/fc-review-results/aea251bb26/#/f/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture23

Erdős 422. The 11 Sept review said Hofstadter's Q-sequence was a partial def, an opaque constant with no equations. FC#5791 replaced it with a predicate IsHofstadterQ f. The 23 Sept review shows (sorry-free) that the predicate refutes EventuallyConst on its own (a constant tail c forces c = 2c), so eventually_const collapsed into "does the recursion ever die", a different question from the docstring's "does f become stationary". The degeneracy was invisible while f was opaque; the fix made the statement analysable and exposed it. https://tadamcz.com/fc-review-results/aea251bb26/#/f/ErdosProblems/422

Tom Adamczewski said:

btw, the OEIS does make me wonder whether additions like FC#6426 or FC#4946 are worth the maintenance burden.

good question. One main reason to add those was to fix the misformalisations that were in the dataset used by Epoch AI and thereby have something that is at least more meaningful than and keep it maintained. I don't think the maintenance burdon will be super high, over all I expect that we will have around 400 problems from the OEIS, but the mid term goal is to have 10k problems altogether, so then they don't have a great weight anymore. And there are some benefits to also have lots of easier (but as of now open) problems in Formal Conjectures.
Work on FC#6426 or FC#4946 is probably not of the highest urgency, but when we do a good review while adding them and are then fairly sure the formalisation is correct, marking them as research solved should be not a huge burdon
Of course that means that FC#6426 or FC#4946 would need to have proper reviews (which is partially already done, but more eyes of agents would be great)
